name: Nagar Van Yojana
benefit:
- The Ministry will provide a one-time development and non-recurring grant of ₹4,00,000/- per hectare.
- The maximum financial assistance for a Nagar Van is limited to ₹2,00,00,000/- for 50 hectares.

_eligibility_text: - The applicant must be a Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Municipality, Urban Local Body, State Forest Department, Educational Institution, University, Government Organisation, or Non-Government Organisation. - The applicant must have possession of the proposed land. - The applicant must provide a commitment to bear the balance cost of the project beyond the provided grant. - The applicant must ensure that the proposed area is situated on forest land or other vacant non-forest public land. - The applicant must formulate a Development cum Management Plan with year-wise details of works under different components. ##### ***For Nagar Van*** - The applicant must develop the Nagar Van over a minimum area of 10 hectares. - The applicant must restrict the maximum area for grant calculation to 50 hectares. - The applicant must ensure the site is located within a 5-kilometre limit of the Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, or Municipality. - The applicant must maintain a minimum of 2/3rd of the Nagar Van area under woodland or tree cover. ##### ***For Nagar Vatika*** - The applicant must develop the Nagar Vatika in a minimum area of 1 hectare. - The applicant must restrict the maximum area of the Nagar Vatika to 10 hectares. - The applicant must ensure the site is located strictly within the city limits or congested parts of the cities. ##### ***Post-Selection Conditions*** - The applicant must keep all Nagar Vans and Nagar Vatikas open and accessible to the city dwellers and general public, subject to suitable restrictions. - The applicant should encourage a Public-Private Partnership mode to ensure the active participation of people, students, and other stakeholders in planning, implementation, and management. - The applicant should select trees from species that are best suited for local conditions. - The applicant should place an emphasis on enriching biodiversity, planting fruit-bearing trees, and cultivating medicinal plants. - The applicant should ensure sufficient revenue generation for maintenance by levying user fees, receiving grants from other agencies, and promoting economic activities like the sale of saplings or processed forest products from the first year. - The applicant should encourage the use of locally available material, energy conservation, and waste recycling.
